newsitem.title: USA: DIRECTV distributor mulls first junk bond offering.
newsitem.headline: DIRECTV distributor mulls first junk bond offering.

text.p: Digital TV Services, a distributor of digital broadcast satellite service DIRECTV, is considering tapping the high-yield market for the first time and has chosen Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp to underwrite the offering, said Donald Doering, the company's chief financial officer.
Doering said the company plans to issue non-cash paying securities such as zero coupon bonds or PIK preferred stock, but was still waiting for the right market conditions.
He said in March the company planned to issue $125 million in senior subordinated discount notes, but postponed the deal due to the correction in the junk bond market.
"The (high-yield) market has improved, but I can't say its (currently) where we want it," he said.
He added the final size and the structure of the planned offering has yet to be determined and declined further comment.

In March, Moody's Investors Service rated Digital TV's proposed deal B3. The agency said, "The ratings reflect the company's negative operating cash flow to date; Moody's expectation that it will incur additional debt to acquire more franchises; and competition from other direct-to-home providers and cable companies."

According to a Moody's statement, "Proceeds from the offering will be used to make pending acquisitions totalling about $25 million, repay $70 million of outstanding bank debt, and leave about $25 million of cash on hand for working capital and future acquisitions."
Digital TV, a privately-held company, is an exclusive distributor of DIRECTV, covering about 1.5 million rural U.S. households. The company, based in Roswell, Georgia, has around 88,000 subscribers.
DIRECTV, a subsidiary of General Motors Corp, is the largest DBS provider in the U.S and has a total of 2.3 million subscribers nationwide.

Pegasus Communications Corp, based in Radnor, Pa, is the only other DIRECTV distributor to have tapped the high-yield market. In January, the company issued $100 million in 12.75 percent cumulative exchangeable PIK preferred stock due '07 via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
